newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten warns China about subversion law.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten warns China about subversion law.

text.p: Hong Kong and the international community would be alarmed if a proposed subversion law was to be scrapped by a China-controlled legislature after Beijing takes over in 1997, Governor Chris Patten said on Sunday.

"I think the community here and the international community would be extremely concerned if the protection of human rights in Hong Kong was to be undermined by decisions taken by an appointed body like the provisional legislature," he told reporters at the airport after returning from a visit to Japan.

Last Tuesday, the colonial government proposed a soft anti-subversion law that would make criticism of the government not a crime to prevent Chinese-style jailings of dissidents after the 1997 handover.

China has condemned the move. "This will only cause disruption and instability in Hong Kong," China's spokesman in Hong Kong Zhang Junsheng said on Friday. Some members of the pro-China lobby predicted the law would be replaced by more Chinese-style legislation after the handover on July 1.
Hong Kong will revert to China at midnight next June 30 and a China-controlled provisional legislature will be installed after the changing of flags.
China, anger by Britain's electoral reform, has vowed to dissolve the elected legislature and replace it with a provisional chamber.
